name: Prairie School
summary: A style of architecture developed in the Midwest United States that emphasized horizontal lines, open floor plans, and integration with the landscape.

name: Forbidden City Architecture
summary: The architectural style of the imperial palaces in China, exemplified by the Forbidden City in Beijing.

name: Analytic Cubism
summary: A phase of Cubism that analyzed objects into geometric planes.

name: Golden Age of Illustration
summary: Period of exceptional illustration characterized by technical mastery and narrative richness in printed media.

name: High Gothic
summary: Mature phase of Gothic architecture marked by increased height, light, and structural refinement.

name: Palladianism
summary: Classical architectural style based on the designs and principles of Andrea Palladio, emphasizing symmetry, proportion, and classical orders.

name: Roman Baroque
summary: A dramatic, theatrical style of architecture characterized by grandeur, movement, and emotional intensity.

name: Neoclassical
summary: An architectural movement reviving the principles of classical Greek and Roman architecture.

name: American Craftsman
summary: A domestic architectural style derived from the Arts and Crafts movement, emphasizing simplicity, natural materials, and craftsmanship.

name: Bungalow/Craftsman
summary: A smaller, single-story version of the American Craftsman style featuring low-pitched roofs, deep porches, and natural materials.

name: Queen Anne (Victorian)
summary: A highly decorative style characterized by asymmetry, variety of textures, and picturesque compositions.

name: Basilica Plan
summary: A rectangular church plan with a central nave flanked by aisles and an apse at one end.

name: Victorian interior
summary: Eclectic interiors combining multiple historical styles with rich ornamentation and dark colors.

name: New American Farmhouse
summary: A contemporary interpretation of traditional American farmhouse style that blends rustic elements with modern amenities and clean lines.

name: Parisian Café
summary: Traditional French cafes serving coffee, alcohol, and light meals in sidewalk settings.

name: Asian electronics design
summary: Design approach in consumer electronics characterized by minimalist forms, advanced interfaces, and integration of traditional aesthetics.

name: Scandinavian design
summary: Democratic Nordic design uniting light woods, functional simplicity, craft quality and egalitarian beauty.

name: Cyberpunk
summary: "High tech, low life": rain-soaked megacity neon, corporate dystopia, chrome implants and street-level tech noir.

name: Pre-Raphaelites
summary: A group of English painters, poets, and critics who formed the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in 1848 to reform art by rejecting what they considered the mechanistic approach of Mannerist artists after Raphael.

name: Fauvism
summary: A style characterized by bold, non-naturalistic colors and expressive brushwork.

name: Synthetic Cubism
summary: A later phase of Cubism that synthesized forms and introduced collage elements.

name: Conceptual Art
summary: Art where the concept or idea behind the work is more important than traditional aesthetic qualities.

name: Literati Painting
summary: A style of painting practiced by scholar-officials in China emphasizing personal expression and scholarly themes.

name: Progressive Artists Group
summary: A group of modern artists who sought to create an Indian modern art language combining international styles with Indian themes.

name: Harlem Renaissance
summary: A cultural explosion centered in Harlem, NYC, celebrating Black identity through literature, music, visual arts, and performance.

name: Arabesque
summary: Intricate interlacing patterns of foliage and geometric forms used in Islamic art and architecture.

name: Hyperrealism
summary: An advancement of Photorealism that creates illusions of reality beyond photographic representation.

name: Early Gothic
summary: The initial phase of Gothic architecture characterized by pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses.

name: Pisan Romanesque
summary: Distinctive variant of Romanesque architecture featuring striped marble decoration and elliptical arches.

name: French Baroque
summary: A more restrained and classical interpretation of Baroque architecture with emphasis on symmetry and grandeur.

name: Gothic Revival
summary: A movement reviving medieval Gothic architectural elements in the 18th and 19th centuries.

name: Colonial Revival
summary: A style that reinterpreted colonial American architecture with classical elements and symmetrical designs.

name: Organic architecture
summary: An architectural philosophy that promotes harmony between human habitation and the natural world.

name: Googie
summary: A space-age architectural style characterized by bold geometric shapes, upswept roofs, and futuristic elements designed to attract automobile traffic.

name: Sustainable/Green Architecture
summary: Architecture designed to minimize environmental impact through energy efficiency, sustainable materials, and integration with natural systems.

name: Dravidian temple
summary: A distinctive South Indian temple architecture characterized by pyramid-shaped towers called vimanas and elaborate gopurams (gateway towers).

name: Inca Ashlar Masonry
summary: Highly precise stonework characterized by tightly fitted polygonal blocks without mortar, exemplifying Inca engineering prowess.

name: Spanish Colonial Architecture
summary: A style derived from Spanish architectural traditions adapted to colonies in the Americas and Asia.

name: Mosque Typology
summary: A diverse architectural tradition for Islamic worship spaces with distinctive spatial and formal elements.

name: Georgian interior
summary: Formal, balanced interiors characterized by symmetry, proportion, and classical elements.

name: Quiet luxury interiors
summary: Un ostentatious luxury focused on quality and craftsmanship

name: American Diner
summary: A type of small restaurant characterized by a long counter with stools and a service rail.

name: Scandinavian Hygge
summary: A cozy interior design aesthetic focused on comfort and contentment through simple, functional spaces.

name: Thonet Bentwood
summary: A furniture style characterized by steam-bent wooden components creating lightweight, curved forms.

name: Tiffany lamps
summary: Stained glass lamps characterized by intricate naturalistic designs and iridescent glass techniques.

name: Industrial Pendant Lighting
summary: Lighting fixtures inspired by factory and warehouse aesthetics featuring raw materials and exposed mechanics.

name: Lunar New Year Visual Traditions
subcategory: East and Southeast Asian new-year visual culture
summary: The lunisolar new year across East and Southeast Asia: red couplets and papercuts, dragon and lion dances, lanterns, hongbao and firecrackers — a chromatic culture ruled by auspicious red and gold.

name: Mid-century modern
summary: Postwar design language of clean organic lines, molded plywood and plastic, optimistic color and indoor-outdoor living.

name: Vaporwave
summary: Internet-born music and visual language of slowed mall music, Roman busts, Windows 95 nostalgia and capitalist ennui.

name: Cottagecore
summary: Idealized rural domesticity: baking, gardening, linen dresses and pastoral calm, amplified by pandemic-era escapism.

name: Bauhaus
summary: The German school and design language that fused art, craft and industry around geometric form, primary colors and functional honesty.

name: Y2K fashion
summary: Turn-of-millennium pop fashion: low-rise jeans, baby tees, butterfly clips, metallics and tech-optimistic shine.

name: Dark Academia
summary: Romanticized scholarly gloom: candlelit libraries, Latin, tweed blazers and gothic campus architecture, mourning beauty and knowledge.

name: Gothic architecture
summary: A structural and spiritual architecture of pointed arches, rib vaults, flying buttresses and walls of stained-glass light.

name: Punk fashion
summary: DIY anti-fashion: safety pins, tartan bondage trousers, leather, torn tees and slogan graphics weaponized as style.

name: Synthwave
summary: 1980s-reviving electronic music and art: neon grids, chrome sunsets, Testarossa dashes and VHS cop-drama mood.

name: Symbolism
summary: A movement that emerged in France in the late 19th century as a reaction against naturalism and realism, emphasizing spiritual and mystical themes.

name: Der Blaue Reiter
summary: An Expressionist group focused on spiritual and abstract forms.

name: Color Field
summary: A style of abstract painting that emerged in the 1950s, characterized by large areas of flat, solid color.

name: Photorealism
summary: Painting and drawing that replicates the appearance of photographs with extreme precision.
